abstract: The genomic characterization of cancers has considerably advanced research and clinical practice. However, critical gaps remain, including limited knowledge of tumor profiles in rare cancers and populations understudied in genomic research and insufficient integration of genomic, clinical and epidemiologic data. This Perspective highlights the Participant Engagement and Cancer Genome Sequencing (PE-CGS) Network, established by the US National Cancer Institute to address knowledge gaps in rare and understudied cancers. PE-CGS comprises five research centers supported by a coordinating center and guided by an external advisory panel. Collaborations across PE-CGS are grounded in shared values of participant-centeredness, engagement, access, collaboration and innovation. Activities emphasize participant engagement throughout the research process, including the return of results and collection of clinical and epidemiologic data alongside paired tumor/germline sequencing. PE-CGS demonstrates how engagement, return of results and comprehensive data collection can be integrated to support participant-centered cancer genomics research and accelerate research in rare and understudied cancers.
